summary:
Systematic Investor Ep.352 (June 2025): Baltas and Kaastrup-Larsen discuss AI/data overload, trend following after the April 2025 V-shape, dynamic volatility targeting and leverage, institutional constraints (Junge article, low beta), Asness on missing the best days, and whether to time trend allocations.
Conclusions: V-shapes hurt every trend speed, leverage into turning points matters, hold trend as a strategic allocation and do not exit after drawdowns.

coverage.note: intro; AI/ML data vendors on radar
data value and alpha decay; LLM unreliability
June 2025 trend performance; April V-shape and speed
V-shape double reversion, client reaction, barometer, index numbers
traditional index numbers, drawdown durations; dynamic vol targets introduced
barometer and diversification; vol targeting schools; V-shape turning points
leverage into turning points; lower vol; why dynamic
loss aversion, hindsight in backtests, barometer vs performance
carry/reversion diversification; dynamic risk budgets; Hedge Nordic intro
Junge article on unconstrained portfolios; mean-variance vs benchmark
low beta and structural constraints; capacity circularity
article conclusions; Asness best days paper
can CTAs be timed; strategic allocation; Nov 2021 loss example
are rules breaking down; systematic vs discretionary; 2025 macro themes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: every other day I get an email about a new data vendor that, you know, simply came up with a new algorithm that somehow tries to extract sentiment or extract alpha
claims.claim: New ML/AI data vendors constantly pitch sentiment and alpha extraction; a systematic firm has to judge the value-add of such data and how long it will persist.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: what are also the best ways of assessing this type of data and assessing the value that you can bring
claims.claim: New data sources need evaluation for alpha and the mechanisms by which that alpha decays over time.
claims.testable: partly: decay can be measured out of sample

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: give me like the 10 most important references that I should go and read on the back end of this paper. complete disaster
claims.claim: LLMs summarise papers well but fabricated references (wrong names and titles), so LLM outputs need verification.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: saying no to uh certain innovations um are as important as saying yes to the right innovations
claims.claim: Rejecting some data and technology innovations is as important as adopting the right ones for systematic managers.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: trends are pretty scar still. Um there are very very few bright points uh or bright spots in the portfolio
claims.claim: In June 2025 trends were scarce; bright spots were unusual ones like lean hogs and live cattle, plus equities (DAX at all-time highs).

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of the long positions um um got cut you know around the low um managers locked in uh losses uh didn't have a lot of exposure
claims.claim: After April 2025 (Liberation Day) equity longs were cut near the low, so managers locked in losses and missed the rebound.
claims.conditions: fast trend followers in sharp V-shaped reversals
claims.testable: yes: signal speed vs P&L in April 2025

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: long-term uh trend followers at least probably and thankfully didn't reverse positions and go short on equities
claims.claim: Longer-term trend followers did not flip short equities in the April 2025 sell-off, unlike shorter-term managers.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: then as it hits kind of some intermediate bottom then it bounces back again. So like two reversions one after the other.
claims.claim: A V-shaped market is two reversals in a row, so trend followers get hit twice, especially quick ones that crystallise losses on both legs.
claims.conditions: fast trend followers lose most in V shapes (Aug 2024 yen, April 2025, SVB in bonds)
claims.testable: yes: loss as function of signal speed

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I'm not sure whether the markets are reacting very different to information I'm not sure if the information in the market is a bit more short-lived and more noisy
claims.claim: Open question whether V-shaped events once a year (SVB 2023, Aug 2024, April 2025) reflect a changed regime of shorter-lived, noisier information.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't think we have seen a crisis year to date or year on year
claims.claim: Trend followers keep their role as crisis hedge; investors stayed because no sustained crisis has occurred, with no outflows and rising inflows.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: my own trend barometer finished at 39 last night
claims.claim: Baltas uses a trend barometer (strength of trends/directional signals); at 39 it signalled weak but stable trends in June 2025.
claims.testable: yes: it is a defined indicator

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: CT index up about 1% uh in June down 7.6% for the year
claims.claim: June 2025 (to Tuesday): BTOP50 +1.17% (-3.39% YTD), SG CTA about +1% (-7.6% YTD), SG Trend +1% (-10.4% YTD), short-term traders -0.64% (-3.32% YTD).
claims.indicator: BTOP50; SG CTA; SG Trend; SG Short-Term Traders

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the S&P 500 00 up 2.2% in June and up 3.29% so far this year
claims.claim: Traditional markets by mid-June 2025: MSCI World +2% in June and +7% YTD; US aggregate bonds flat (+2.31% YTD); S&P 500 +2.2% in June and +3.29% YTD.
claims.indicator: MSCI World; S&P 500; US aggregate bond index

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: some managers are somewhat further away in time from their all-time highs
claims.claim: Some CTAs last made all-time highs in 2022; CTA replicators were also in long drawdowns by mid-2025.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: building a strategy with some inputs in terms of signaling some inputs in terms of risk call it cover structure or something along those lines
claims.claim: Trend portfolios are built from signals plus a risk model (vol and correlation estimates) and usually target or bound portfolio volatility so investors can scale them next to 60/40.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there could be value in changing dynamically through time that level of volatility that is targeted
claims.claim: Idea: make the portfolio-level volatility target dynamic instead of constant, because realized volatility is a function of leverage, which depends on diversification and correlation.
claims.testable: yes: backtest dynamic vs static target

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if your barometer is 90%. Then more likely than not you have a lot of directional exposures
claims.claim: A high trend barometer means directional, concentrated exposure (equity or rate risk); a low barometer means mixed positions, more diversification, lower correlation and higher leverage needed to hit a vol target.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you have the school of people targeting um VAR
claims.claim: Three risk-sizing schools: target volatility, target VaR with a risk budget, or fix initial risk and let VaR float; some managers' portfolio vol swung from 30 to 90 in a year, which Niels calls wild.
claims.indicator: vol target vs VaR vs fixed risk

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: however quick or slow you are the turning point is a turning point
claims.claim: No trend speed avoids turning-point losses: slow followers ride the whole V, fast ones lose less going down but recover less, so trajectories differ but all lose.
claims.testable: yes: simulate speeds through V events

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there is no predictability of the turning point. So the question then becomes how led are you entering into that point
claims.claim: Because turning points are unpredictable, leverage going into them matters: twice the leverage means roughly double the loss.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: are those environments uh inviting us to consider lower levels of leverage and other in other words lower levels of volatility
claims.claim: If V-shapes become more frequent and signal-to-noise is low, lower volatility targets (less leverage) may be warranted.
claims.direction: lower leverage when signal-to-noise is low
claims.testable: partly: hard to detect regime in real time

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the levels of realized v are slightly lower than what historically was the case you know they maybe fluctuate between 7 and 10 or 11 and historically you can see values between 10 and 12 or 13
claims.claim: SG Trend index realized volatility over the last 1-2 years was about 7-11%, below the historic 10-13%, hinting managers already run lower or more dynamic risk.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we would say well it must be because then they can maybe reduce some of the draw downs and maybe they can make you know have more risk on when there are you know lots of trends
claims.claim: Motivation for dynamic vol targets: cut drawdowns and take more risk when trends are plentiful; open question is how managers decide the level.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we value less $1 of a gain than the pain we experience if we lose $1
claims.claim: Loss aversion (prospect theory) motivates reducing leverage during drawdowns: an investor prefers being under-levered in a loss at the cost of upside.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: any type of kind of past performance adjustment will perhaps show us better performance recently because guess what we kind of know how it went
claims.claim: Dynamic de-leveraging after losses will look good on recent episodes through hindsight, but backtests would show cases where lower exposure to emerging trends hurt; it is a trade-off, not a free lunch.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: historically there is no association between the overall trendiness or your barometer to subsequent performance except when this is too high
claims.claim: Historically trend strength (barometer) does not predict subsequent trend performance, except that very high trendiness precedes underperformance because the trends share few principal components.
claims.direction: reduce risk/take profits when barometer very high

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: year to date all those other components have actually been extremely extremely helpful at least from my perspective uh to diversify those trend exposures
claims.claim: In 2025 carry and mean-reversion components diversified trend exposures well without reducing correlation to the benchmark.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we've also introduced kind of dynamic risk uh budgeting uh more than 12 years ago now and and we from our point obviously find it very valuable
claims.claim: Niels's firm has used dynamic risk budgeting for over 12 years and sees value in it, using volatility and correlations beyond price; critics call it contrary to pure trend following.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: not all trend followers are the same
claims.claim: The 12-14 months after 2024 revealed differences in risk budgeting and design among trend followers that look correlated in normal times.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if you just take a minor optimizer and you have a 60/40 portfolio and managed features you should do 100% managed features and zero 6040
claims.claim: Mean-variance would put 100% in managed futures (higher Sharpe), but investors are judged against a benchmark, so career and tracking-error risk constrain the allocation.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: in reality there's so many constraints in place people try to be sensitive to costs makes sense they try to be conscious about liquidity
claims.claim: Institutional constraints (liquidity, governance, regulation, leverage limits, benchmarks, reputation) confine the portfolio space; an unconstrained investor would hold more private equity, CTAs, infrastructure.
claims.testable: no: thought piece (Christoph Junge article, Hedge Nordic)

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the fact that low beta stocks outperform is largely driven by the fact that we have capacity or leverage constraints
claims.claim: The low-beta anomaly comes from leverage constraints (investors cannot lever a 1% vol stock 10x) and benchmark hugging, which bids up high beta and lowers its returns.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we cannot take for granted an expected return
claims.claim: Alternatives' historical returns partly exist because allocations are small; larger inflows could cause capacity issues and lower returns, a circular dependence.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you better stay invested because what if you missed the 10 best days of of the S&P
claims.claim: Cliff Asness's paper argues the 'miss the 10 best days' argument is misleading, since someone missing the best days would also miss some of the worst; the April 2025 tariff pause produced one of the best S&P days in decades.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Maybe we should rethink how we um how we reward success
claims.claim: The article argues institutions should rethink how success is rewarded and the tolerance for short-term risk of long-term investors.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if it's indeed some sort of a uh statistical insurance, there's clearly no way for for anyone to time it and it has to be a strategic decision
claims.claim: Trend following should be a strategic allocation (like insurance), because timing it is not possible: past performance is a weak predictor of future returns.
claims.testable: yes: test timing rules on trend indices

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: most of the outperforming periods of trend following kind of started with like a slowdown or some underperformance
claims.claim: Analyses by Katy Kaminski (AlphaSimplex) and Man Group show trend-following outperformance often began after a stretch of underperformance, so exiting after losses is the worst decision.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: a loss of a certain amount creates more pain than a gain of the same amount
claims.claim: Moderating risk through vol scaling is distinct from timing the allocation in and out: it manages the pain of losses at the margin.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the last or second last trading day of November 2021 just
claims.claim: A big one-day CTA loss in late November 2021 looked like a reason to exit but preceded the very strong 2022; a five-month losing run can be followed by a great month, so unpredictable.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't think you can find daily skew positive daily skew in trend following strate like because they look into longer term windows
claims.claim: Trend following does not show positive skew at daily frequency, only over longer windows, so judging it day to day is unfair; discipline and expectation-setting matter.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: most of the trend investors year to date have not actually responded to this Vshape is partly an acknowledgement that you know we know why it's there
claims.claim: Most trend investors did not change models after the 2025 V-shape since this is the known losing regime; its sign is understood, only the size is in question.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: have the markets changed you know have the world stopped following rules so to speak
claims.claim: Hedge Nordic editorial question: markets moving on tweets and statements may mean trend rules are breaking down or merely paused; whether to add discretionary input.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: how would we know that S&P would have one of the three largest returns in 50 years on that uh post day
claims.claim: Information shocks like the April 2025 tariff pause cannot be foreseen or captured by systematic signals; at such times signals are noisy.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: a falling growth and perhaps um um a relatively bound um rangebound trajectory for for yields and inflation
claims.claim: Baltas's 2025 macro read: falling growth with range-bound yields and inflation pointed to being out of equities, long gold or a curve steepener, themes that played out but were missed by fast systematic signals.
claims.indicator: growth; yields; inflation; gold; curve steepener

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I don't think we should emotionally react. Agree. But I do not think we should be dogmatic
claims.claim: Stance on the debate: do not react emotionally to a bad run but stay open to evolving the models.
